$comment: The digs ledger. This library is built by repeated passes over our own history,
and the first pass is nowhere near all of it.
Every idea carries `source: <dig id>`. That makes 'what did this pass actually yield?'
a query instead of an archaeology project, and it keeps the library honest about being
incomplete: STATUS.md renders this as a board with the outstanding rows visible.
Note on what belongs in `detail`: describe the KIND of material, never where it lives,
how much of it there is, or how sensitive it is. An earlier version of this file named
volumes and flagged which source was riskiest, which amounted to publishing a map of
our own unscrubbed material. The board's purpose survives without any of that.
`yield` is written by scripts/build.mjs from the actual idea count — never by hand.

digs.label: Hand-written exemplars
digs.detail: The first ideas, written by hand to set the quality bar for everything after.

digs.label: Project registry
digs.detail: Projects already catalogued in a structured form, so the cheapest pass to run first.

digs.label: Working directories
digs.detail: Project folders that never made it into the registry. Expect the same idea under several names; dedupe against existing ids.

digs.label: Published repositories
digs.detail: Work that is already public. Lowest risk and highest link value, since each entry can cite its own repo.

digs.label: Older work
digs.detail: Things set aside long enough to have an outcome. Expect dead ideas, which are the most valuable kind here.

digs.label: Discussed but never built
digs.detail: Ideas that were considered, decided against, or tried once and never got a folder. The only source for `idea-only` entries.

digs.label: Published listings
digs.detail: Things listed on somebody else's storefront, with real usage numbers attached.

digs.label: On-chain history
digs.detail: Contracts and tokens deployed. Chain state is measurable evidence, so these entries can carry high-confidence verdicts.

digs.label: Outside contributions
digs.detail: Ideas and corrections contributed by people who are not us. Open-ended, permanently.
